tier_reason: Enrichment found the record mixed ADBench (peer-reviewed, Adept 1.1 era) with Xcelerit ad-benchmarks; claim restated from ad-benchmarks, tier B kept pending a check of that suite's flags.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Xcelerit ad-benchmarks (GCC 13.3, Xeon 8488C, run by the XAD vendor): Adept 2 beats CppAD on all 4 rows (e.g. Heston 91 vs 268 ms) and loses to XAD on all 4; ADBench (OMS 2018, Adept 1.1) showed gains over ADOL-C on GMM (1.8x unsplit).
corrections.caveats: Two sources were mixed in the original record (ad-benchmarks for workload/hardware, ADBench for the speedup); ad-benchmarks is vendor-run by XAD's maker.

tier_reason: Tier C kept; hardware corrected by enrichment.

corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X (Zen4, AVX-512 path); AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 5975WX (AVX2 path); Apple M2 Max (NEON)

corrections.caveats: The MpGEMM authors' code is now public at github.com/mpgemm/MPGEMM (MIT), so 'authors released no code' is stale.
Correction: 'T=50' is the action horizon; FlashRT's DiT also runs 4 denoising steps like NVIDIA's table. RTX 5090 rows are CUDA-graph replay only and exclude pre/postprocessing and transfers.

tier_reason: Enrichment found the AVX-512 kernel computes wrong results for half of each call's transforms (DK macro fills 16 lanes with 8 values, lanes 8-15 get zero twiddles); numbers measured on code with an unfixed correctness bug go to C (lessons). The AVX2 path was not shown faulty.

corrections.caveats: AVX-512 path bug: lanes 8-15 use zero twiddle constants, so half the transforms are wrong; tests print only lane 0. Treat AVX-512 numbers as unverified.

tier_reason: Enrichment found the harness not reproducible as shipped: the host loads fft_4096_mma.metal, which is not in the repo, and the kernel that produces the headline is mis-described (comment claims simdgroup MMA, code runs scalar butterflies). Public code that does not run as published does not meet tier A.

corrections.caveats: Host loads a missing fft_4096_mma.metal; the headline kernel runs scalar radix-8 butterflies despite its MMA comment; Metal fastMath on.

tier_reason: Published benchmark images (2024-05-03) predate correctness fix b15d5e2 (2024-05-09: last triangle around a constrained edge not always Delaunay); project rule puts numbers measured on code later fixed for correctness at C until re-measured.
Flags now known from the benchmarking-fft Makefile, but the CPU model is still not stated, so the tier stays C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: SIMD build: g++ -O3 -march=native -std=c++20 plus about 15 opt-in tuning macros (POCKETFFT_TUNED_DEFINES); no-SIMD build: clang++ -O3 with vectorization off (benchmarking-fft Makefile). FFTW 3.3.10 built from the release tarball; KFR 7 built with clang++ C++20.

tier_reason: First-party; the query half of the claim timed an inexact search (far-child pruning compares a linear gap to a squared distance), so only the build claim stands.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: construction about 15 percent faster than nanoflann. The README's 'nearest neighbor query about 10 percent faster' is invalid: the search over-prunes (linear gap vs squared distance) and returns wrong neighbours, and benchmark.cpp never checks results.

tier_reason: First-party; build comparison inflated by a double nanoflann build in the timed loop.

corrections.caveats: The 2.6x build ratio is inflated: bm_nanoflann.cpp builds the nanoflann index twice in the timed loop (constructor already calls buildIndex() since nanoflann 1.4); real build gap is about 1.3x (estimate). kNN numbers are unaffected.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed FGCS 2021 numbers unchanged; record description corrected.

corrections.caveats: ALBUS uses plain CSR with no format conversion; preprocessing is only a thread partition. Kernel reads one double past rows of length 3 mod 4; repo bench runs cache-warm and ignores the iterations argument.

tier_reason: First-party; exponential figure measured on a generator with a correctness bug.

corrections.caveats: The exponential generator has a cast bug (ke[0]=0) that sends every base-strip draw to the tail, so its 5.2x figure was timed on a wrong distribution; the normal (7.4x) and uniform (4.7x) figures are unaffected. RcppZiggurat carries the same line.
Recount from summary.md: versus CPU AMGCL apxchol is faster on 18 of 27 matrices, tied on 3 and slower on 6 (the earlier '21 of 27' overstated it). Factors are not repeatable across thread counts.
